identity.title: Kussmaul sign: JVP rises (or fails to fall) with inspiration

technique.how: Position the patient so the top of the jugular venous column is visible (usually 30-45 degrees), identify the JVP and its meniscus, then ask for a slow deep inspiration through the mouth. Normally the column falls; Kussmaul sign is present when it fails to fall or rises with inspiration.
technique.prerequisites: Visible JVP (exclude hepatojugular pressure); patient able to breathe deeply on command.

interpretation.positive_finding: A positive sign indicates impaired right-heart filling with inspiration - RV infarction in the setting of inferior MI (LR+ about 6), constrictive pericarditis, severe RV failure/pulmonary hypertension, or massive PE; it is classically absent in pure tamponade.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence lowers the probability of RV infarction in inferior MI (LR- about 0.2) but does not exclude constriction or RV failure; it says little about tamponade, where the sign is usually absent anyway.
interpretation.pitfalls: Requires a visible JVP - obesity, a very high JVP above the mandible, or shallow breathing hide it. Kussmaul sign with pulsus paradoxus suggests effusive-constrictive disease rather than simple tamponade.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive in inferior MI: obtain right-sided ECG leads/echo and avoid preload reduction (nitrates, diuretics); positive with oedema/ascites: pursue constriction or RV failure by echo.

estimates.target_condition: Right ventricular myocardial infarction in patients admitted with acute inferior myocardial infarction
estimates.population: 469 consecutive patients with acute inferior MI, pooled from 8 diagnostic-accuracy studies (1965-2019 literature)
estimates.reference_standard: Combined reference standards across studies (echocardiography, haemodynamics, ECG/angiography as defined per study)
estimates.quote: Kussmaul's sign had a sensitivity of 62.5% (44.6, 77.5), specificity 90% (73.0, 96.8), negative likelihood ratio (LR) 0.2 (0.1-0.8) and positive LR 5.8 (2.5, 13.3)

sources.citation: Dube E, Crozier M, Middleton A, Best B, Ohle R. Kussmaul's sign for the diagnosis of right ventricular myocardial infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy studies. CJEM. 2021.
Adler Y, Charron P, Imazio M, Badano L, Baron-Esquivias G, Bogaert J, Brucato A, Gueret P, et al. 2015 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of pericardial diseases. Eur Heart J. 2015.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use to diagnose or exclude tamponade, and do not rely on it when the JVP cannot be seen.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Kussmaul sign with hypotension and clear lungs in inferior MI = RV infarction: give fluids cautiously, avoid nitrates/diuretics, and expedite reperfusion; with muffled sounds and pulsus paradoxus consider effusive-constrictive disease and urgent echo.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No interobserver reliability estimate located; the pooled studies used unblinded bedside assessment in most cases (unverified recall).

extraction_notes: The only diagnostic-accuracy evidence found is for RV infarction complicating inferior MI (Dube 2021, CJEM; not open access, so only abstract-level numbers are quoted; prevalence 'Prevalence of right ventricular myocardial infarction was 36% (confidence interval [CI] 95% 31.8-40.5)', Abstract). Differentials 'acs' and 'cardiogenic_shock' added from vocab to map this target. For constrictive pericarditis, tamponade and RV failure no diagnostic-accuracy study was found (searches 'Kussmaul sign constrictive pericarditis diagnostic accuracy' and 'Kussmaul sign'); the constrictive-pericarditis role rests on the 2015 ESC pericardial guideline (PMID 26320112), whose abstract is empty in e-utils so no page can be cited. Duvalyan 2024 (PMID 38708596) is a POCUS case description, not an accuracy study.
